CHIEF COMPLAINT
Acne on the face.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Kayla Ward is a 19-year-old female presenting with acne located on the face that started approximately two years ago and is present most every day. She has been using Persa-Gel and washing regularly, which she reports is somewhat helpful. She denies associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain. Patient reports acne does not flare with her menstrual cycle. She has had a regular menstrual period for approximately two years. Mother reports that the biggest flare occurred when she started school sports in the fall, likely due to sweating. Mother notes patient has been doing a good job with her facial care regimen but it has not helped as much as desired. Current skin care routine: mornings consist of wiping face with water and washcloth, sometimes using ELF cleanser if face feels greasy; evenings consist of using ELF Super Clarity Cleanser, toner, and Persa-Gel. Today is described as a "good day" for the patient's acne.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies itching, bleeding, or pain from acne. Chest and back acne reported as mild. Regular menstrual periods. Remainder of review of systems not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No additional past medical history.

MEDICATIONS
ELF Super Clarity Cleanser, toner, Persa-Gel, sunscreen SPF 30 (used in summer).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
No additional family history.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with parents and sister. Pets include a dog, bird, and bunnies. Currently in 7th grade. Plays basketball, volleyball, and tap dance. Wears sunscreen SPF 30 in the summer.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Full exam performed except under underwear and bra. Multiple benign nevi on trunk and extremities. Scattered skin-colored papules. Open and closed comedones. Erythematous papules on face, primarily on forehead with some on central cheeks and chin. Chest and back relatively spared. Remainder of examination normal.

RESULTS
Multiple benign moles noted on arms, legs, back, and abdomen with no worrisome features.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Mild to moderate acne, mostly comedonal with small inflammatory component.

Plan: 
1. Morning routine: Wash face with mild cleanser and apply noncomedogenic moisturizer with SPF 30 or higher.
2. Evening routine: Wash face with same cleanser, allow to dry, apply adapalene 0.1% cream in thin layer to areas of acne starting a few nights per week and gradually increasing to nightly use. If adapalene is expensive or not covered by insurance, consider alternative OTC gel. Follow with Clean and Clear Persa-Gel in thin layer and noncomedogenic moisturizer.
3. Wear sunscreen when outside due to sensitivity from adapalene.
4. Counsel regarding potential dryness or irritation from adapalene.
5. Follow-up visit in 6 months to assess progress.
6. Patient instructed to call office with any questions or concerns before next visit.
